record.original_question: If U and V are real analytic domains in C^n, not assumed pseudoconvex, and f:U -> V is biholomorphic, does f extend continuously to the closure U-bar?

evidence.quote: Problem 9.4.1 Does f have a continuous extension to Ū ? (This is true if U, V are pseudoconvex.) 9.5 Stein manifolds

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $U, V \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be bounded domains whose boundaries are real analytic hypersurfaces, and assume neither $U$ nor $V$ is required to be pseudoconvex. Suppose $f \colon U \to V$ is a biholomorphic map. Does $f$ necessarily extend to a continuous map $\overline{f} \colon \overline{U} \to \overline{V}$ on the closure of $U$?
artifact.status_search_result: Boundary regularity of biholomorphisms is well understood in the pseudoconvex real-analytic case (smooth, indeed holomorphic, extension across the boundary). For domains with real-analytic boundary that are not assumed pseudoconvex, the continuous extension question does not appear to be definitively resolved in the literature surveyed; recent works study extensions via abstract boundary constructions but do not provide a general affirmative or negative answer. Status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Biholomorphic mapping - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: For pseudoconvex domains with real-analytic boundary one has holomorphic extension to a neighbourhood of the closure.
status_evidence.claim: The pseudoconvex real-analytic case is solved; the non-pseudoconvex case is not discussed as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Abstract Boundaries and Continuous Extension of Biholomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Different constructions of abstract boundaries... with applications to extension results concerning biholomorphic maps.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work uses abstract boundaries to obtain partial extension results, suggesting the general question remains active.
